about.title: Azusa Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Azusa sits at the base of the San Gabriel Mountains, where local streets like Arrow Highway and Azusa Avenue feed into a busy stretch of the I-210 Foothill Freeway. Recent public records show 190 injury collisions in a single year here, with Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. seeing the heaviest volume as commuters and weekend traffic overlap. If you were injured in one of these crashes, the aftermath can be disorienting — medical visits, missed work, calls from insurance adjusters. We're here to help. Our team can review the details of what happened and explain your options. We work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover. The sooner evidence from the scene is preserved, the stronger a claim tends to be, so reaching out early matters.

whyChoose.title: Why Choose Us for Your Azusa Car Accident Claim

items.title: California's Two-Year Clock
items.desc: California law generally gives you two years from the crash date to file a personal injury lawsuit, but that window can shrink to as little as six months if a government entity — like a city road crew or a public transit vehicle — was involved. We can help you sort out which deadline applies to your situation.

items.title: Comparative Fault Still Pays
items.desc: Even if you're told you were partly at fault, California's pure comparative fault rule means you may still recover damages reduced by your share of responsibility. Insurers sometimes use partial fault to discourage claims entirely, which is why having someone review the facts on your behalf matters.

items.title: No Cap, No Recorded Statement Trap
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering, so these losses can be a meaningful part of a claim. Before giving a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer, it's worth talking to us, since those statements are often used to minimize what you're owed.

items.question: I was hurt in a crash on Azusa Avenue — what should I do first?
items.answer: Seek medical attention even if injuries seem minor, since some symptoms show up later. Try to document the scene with photos and get contact information for any witnesses. From there, our team can help you understand next steps before you talk to any insurance company.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a car accident in Azusa?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the accident to file a personal injury lawsuit. If a government vehicle or road hazard was involved, that deadline can be as short as six months, so it's important to act quickly to preserve your options.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's usually best to avoid giving a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney. Insurance adjusters sometimes use those statements to shift blame or downplay injuries, and we can help protect your interests during that conversation.
